clue.text: Manager contracted by Switzerland's engineering firm

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the word for manager loses its final letter

parts.note: a boss is a manager
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A Swiss boss is hired on contract by an engineering company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like hiring, but it means shortened: BOSS loses its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosch is a large German engineering and electronics company.

clue.text: Sounds of disapproval when intoxicating liquor's picked up

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as a sound heard rather than letters written

parts.note: booze is intoxicating liquor; 'liquor's' gives the possessive booze's

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers when someone reaches for the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Booze's, said aloud, matches the jeering noise of an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers from an audience expressing displeasure are called boos.

clue.text: Unfortunately, peat's too wet for tropical plant

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener laments that the soil is too soggy to grow a warm-climate crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet potato is a tuber-bearing vine native to tropical America.

clue.text: Marsupial overturned in grass brings us cheer

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word reads backwards

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial

explanation.surface: A kangaroo flipped onto its back in the hay makes everyone shout for joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooray is an exclamation of delight, a shout of joy.

clue.text: Brief observed after leader in Scotland showed respect formally

indicators.note: after places the word for observed following the Scottish letter

parts.note: curt means brief, abrupt

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of Scotland

parts.note: eyed means looked at, observed

explanation.surface: A short visitor bows before the head of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtsey is to bend the knees as a formal gesture of deference, typically by a woman.

clue.text: Odd bits of crabs I'm hesitant to put in fish dish

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters of crabs
to put in means the hesitation is inserted inside the fish

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
er is the sound of a hesitant speaker

explanation.surface: A cook is unsure about adding crab pieces to a fish recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' sits in the surface as food, but it only supplies the flatfish whose letters are split by the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew baked in a covered pot, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Our leader casually cycled from the Emerald Isle

indicators.note: cycled means the first letter rides round to the back of the word

parts.note: the Emerald Isle is Ireland, so something from there is Irish

explanation.surface: The prime minister arrives on a bicycle from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving I from the front of IRISH to the end gives the answer. Rishi Sunak was UK prime minister when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi is the first name of Rishi Sunak, informally referring to the then British prime minister.

clue.text: Start introducing enchanting lady to lad

indicators.note: introducing means putting one thing inside the other

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy
a witch casts enchantments

explanation.surface: A first date begins with a charming woman being introduced to a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch on is to turn on a device, getting it going.

clue.text: Reported one that's fleeced crossword solver

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the sheep word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep, which carries a fleece

explanation.surface: A news item says a puzzle fan was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeced' suggests cheated; here it means bearing wool.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the person solving as the second-person pronoun, the reader.

clue.text: Acting as decision maker resolved dispute in golf

indicators.note: resolved here means broken up and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A referee settles a quarrel on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputising means standing in for a superior, taking on that person's authority temporarily.

clue.text: Difficult to bear duck in a stew, but not heart

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: but not heart means the central letter of the anxious word is dropped

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be anxious or nervous

explanation.surface: A troublesome job: cooking a duck in a stew without its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' and 'stew' suggest cookery; 'in a stew' is the idiom for worried, NERVOUS, which loses its middle V.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome, heavy to carry out.

clue.text: Stint carrying Jack half-cut up snow-covered track

indicators.note: carrying means holding the following letters inside

parts.note: to stint is to skimp, be sparing
J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: half-cut means only half of the word up survives, its first letter

explanation.surface: A drunk lumberjack carries on up the snowy trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims up to its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jump is a steep snowy ramp down which skiers race before launching into the air.

clue.text: Team rush around? Sum up business benefit

indicators.note: around means the pair is turned to read the other way

parts.note: a side is a team
to dart is to rush
to count up is to total, to sum up

explanation.surface: A squad hurries about, then tallies the profits.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade discount is a price reduction given by a supplier to another business, a commercial advantage.

clue.text: A French worker pinching this setter's alcohol is petty

indicators.note: pinching means gripping something between, so the setter's drink sits within

parts.note: un is French for a
an ant is the classic worker insect
the setter speaking of themself: I'm, I am
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A French labourer stealing the setter's drink is a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' reads as stealing, but it means the French article and the insect grip the setter's drink between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something petty is trivial, of little significance.

clue.text: Minor route leading to sheds for sows

parts.note: in Britain a B road is a minor route, below an A road
a snake casts, sheds, its skin

explanation.surface: A farmer finds a country lane that runs to the outbuildings where pigs are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sows' looks like female pigs, but it is the verb: a farmer sows seed broadcast by scattering it.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely by hand, sowing it.

clue.text: Bird beginning to leave small stream

indicators.note: the beginning, the first letter, departs from the stream word

parts.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: A bird starts to fly away from a little creek.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black crow-family bird that nests in colonies.

clue.text: Patriot regularly backed by politicians making speeches

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front
regularly takes every other letter: the second, fourth and sixth of patriot

parts.note: Tories are British Conservative politicians

explanation.surface: A patriot is routinely supported by party figures giving addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' looks like support from the politicians, but 'backed' alone is the signal to turn the picked letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Orations are formal public addresses, and the plural of oratory can also mean such pieces of rhetoric.

clue.text: Gathered fool ran after me going north

indicators.note: after sets the word for ran behind the turned me

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: dyes that ran bled

explanation.surface: A crowd came together after an idiot ran north past the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled means brought together, collected into one place.

clue.text: That woman's atop church, the Spanish stargazer

indicators.note: atop places the first piece above the next in a down clue

parts.note: hers means belonging to that woman
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman stands on a church roof watching the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel was the astronomer who discovered Uranus; Caroline, his sister, was an astronomer too.

clue.text: Knowledge of areas circulating with news

indicators.note: circulating means moving around, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Local information spreads along with the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is consciousness of facts, being informed about something.

clue.text: Unsettled about holding exercise class

indicators.note: holding means containing the following inside

parts.note: on means about, concerning
PE is physical education, school exercise lessons

explanation.surface: A wavering instructor is unsure about running the gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: An open question is undecided, still to be resolved.

clue.text: Snitch exposed ring, supporting spy boss

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the inside of ring

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A grass reveals the network that serves the intelligence chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone is to tell tales, to snitch to the authorities.

clue.text: Pit-worker beyond angry recalled dismissal he questions

indicators.note: beyond places the mine worker after the rest

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: getting the axe means being dismissed
a miner works in a coal pit

explanation.surface: A collier is furious after being brought back from the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-examiner interrogates a witness in court on behalf of the opposing side.

clue.text: 10-0 upset that makes little contribution to atmosphere

definitions.text: that makes little contribution to atmosphere

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: zero is none, nothing

explanation.surface: A lopsided ten-nil result in a match does little for the mood in the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas present in the air only in trace amounts.

clue.text: Editor grumpy scratching bottom that's irritable

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the posterior word is removed

parts.note: rump is a bottom, the backside

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered editor scratches his behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and nervous, easily annoyed.

clue.text: Some characters involved with artiste, phenomenal man

indicators.note: some letters within the following words spell the name

explanation.surface: A cast of characters works with a brilliant performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a male first name, so it stands for any man.

clue.text: Death from top falling in cave

indicators.note: the top letter of the down word drops lower in the word

parts.note: a den is a cave or lair

explanation.surface: Someone dies when the roof of a cavern collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the top is the first letter: D falls to the bottom of DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a termination, used of a life it means its close.

clue.text: Guided around old reservation, almost spotted camouflaged beast

indicators.note: around means the guide word goes round the rest

parts.note: led means guided

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a park is land reserved for wildlife

explanation.surface: A guide on a game reserve almost spotted a hidden big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like seen, but it belongs to the definition: a big cat with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large cat whose spotted coat blends into dappled forest light.

clue.text: Names of three chaps removed from play

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the answer splits into Sid, Eli and Ned, three men's names
second meaning: taken out of the action, benched

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: the answer splits into SID, ELI and NED, three men's names.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelined player is kept out of the game, on the bench.

clue.text: Intimate time back in office admitted by former prime minister

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside the prime minister's name

parts.note: Theresa May was UK prime minister 2016-19

indicators.note: the back of office is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cosy moment back in office is let in by an ex-premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey means friendly and familiar, as between close companions.
